source.dirtyPolicy: not applicable; the script archives the committed HEAD via `git archive`, so uncommitted changes never ship (a dirty workspace only triggers a warning)

operations.name: deploy:init
preconditions: reachable SSH host with the dedicated WSL key
guard absent or identical to {targetId: ad, phase: production, lifecycleRevision: 1}
proof: remote guard file equals target ad, production, lifecycle revision 1 (read and compared before any mutation)
recovery: remove the non-secret guard file only before any release uses lifecycle revision 1

operations.name: deploy:code
preconditions: exclusive target lock (mkdir-based, fails immediately if held)
git archive of the commit, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm build` (VITE_WEBPOOL_API_URL = target apiUrl) succeed in a native Linux WSL staging directory (not DrvFs)
an alwaysdata static site whose root is ~/www/datapool (target-authoritative, configured in the admin, never deployed by this script)
~/www/webpool.env present on the target and its WEBPOOL_API_CORS_ORIGINS contains the siteUrl origin (read on the target by node; only that key leaves the file, never DATABASE_URL nor provider keys)
proof: find over ~/www/datapool.new reports no directory other than 755 and no file other than 644
~/www/datapool.new holds index.html and the generated .htaccess (SPA fallback, CSP with the inline script hashes of index.html)
after the swap, GET siteUrl/ and siteUrl/pools answer 200 with exactly the generated Content-Security-Policy
recovery: swap ~/www/datapool.old back over ~/www/datapool; ~/www/datapool.old is only purged at the START of the next deploy:code, so it survives until then
